chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man was asked: He has wealth due from another man on credit, which he had specified for him. When the payment became due, the debtor did not have what to give him. So he wanted to turn it over for him and profit from it: should he sell him pearls and other things worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, and delay the payment? He said: There is no problem with that. My father did that, may Allah be pleased with him, and he ordered me to do that with regard to anything that was due to him.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to Ibrahim ibn al-Harith or Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, depending on the specific lineage context in al-Kafi)
key_terms.عِينَة: Credit sale or deferred payment transaction
key_terms.لُؤْلُؤاً: Pearls (used here as an example of valuable goods)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods on credit at a higher price to recover a debt when the debtor cannot pay immediately?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi validates the practice of 'in'ah' (or 'tadlil'), where a creditor sells a debt for a higher price on credit to recover funds when the debtor is insolvent. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms its permissibility by citing the precedent of his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS), establishing a practical legal mechanism for debt recovery in early Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, form Mas’ada Bin sadaqa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man asked him<sup>asws</sup>, and for him was some wealth upon a man from on credit which he had lent to him. So when the (payment) of the goods was due upon him, he did not give it to him. So he wanted that it be turned over for him, and he would profit him. Can he sell a pearl or other than that what would be equal to one hundred Dirhams, from one thousand Dirhams and delay it (the payment)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that. My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> had done that, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Please with him<sup>asws</sup>, and had instructed me<sup>asws</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> should do that with regards to anything which was upon him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 48. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from those who narrated to him from ‘Amr ibn abu al-Miqdam from al-Harith ibn Hadirah al-Azdiy who has said the following:

“A man during the time of ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had found a treasure and my father bought it from him for three hundred dirham and one hundred sheep followed by their young; and my mother blamed him for it, saying, ‘You have bought it for three hundred sheep; one hundred of their young, one hundred sheep and one hundred in their womb.’ My father regretted and went to ask for a reduced price. He refused and said, ‘Take from me ten sheep, take from me twenty sheep’ and made him tired. My father then took the treasure and made a price for one thousand sheep from it. The other man came back and said, ‘Take your sheep back and give me whatever you like.’ But he refused. He tried until he was exhausted and said, ‘I can harm you.’ He complained before ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, against my father. When my father told his side of the story before ’Amir al- Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, he (the Imam) said to the owner of treasure, ‘Pay one-fifth of what you have received because it is on you as the finder of the treasure and there is nothing on him because he has taken the price of his sheep.’”
